value.first: Right on time - 6 months is exactly when to start. The method is iron-first solids with early allergen introduction: babies run low on iron around now, and the big trials (LEAP, EAT) showed feeding allergens early cuts allergy risk sharply rather than waiting. Look for readiness first: sitting steady in a high chair with good head control, opening up when food comes.
value.second: Day 1: sit him fully upright, offer a spoon or two of one iron-rich food - iron-fortified oat cereal mixed with milk, pureed beef, or mashed lentils. Most ends up on the tray, that's a win. Days 2-7: build to iron-rich food twice a day, add mashed veg and fruit. Milk continues as usual. Gagging is noisy and normal; it's not choking. Never honey before 12 months.
value.third: Week 2, allergens: thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter into a puree (never a glob), give a taste, wait 10 min, watch two hours. Next day, cooked egg. Then one new allergen a day - egg, dairy, wheat, soy, sesame, fish. Once tolerated, keep it in about twice a week. If he ever gets trouble breathing, swelling, or widespread hives after eating, that's an emergency - go now. Emma Hubbard, a paediatric OT, has a solid starting-solids walkthrough. I'll check in Thursday.
